messages.subject: problem with the calculation
parts:
hi i have a phenotype that has 1 in all the observations when i run RQTL
with simple marker regression in the scanone command i get high lod scores when it should be zero
i dont understand why....when i try other methods like binary or EM it gives me the zero as expected in the LOD SCORE column


elad

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] problem with the calculation
parts:
R/qtl doesn't check to see whether a phenotype column is all 0's.

The LOD score is a comparison between the residual sum of squares (RSS) when fitting just an intercept to the RSS when fitting a QTL model. In the case you mention, these should both be 0, but if one is 10^-23 and the other is 10^-24, you'll get spurious results.

karl
